description:
## Goal Build the Collaboration locks example in examples/collaboration/. This is the most technically complex example. It demonstrates a Document.Server that combines two Filament capabilities: pessimistic locking (Filament.Hold — one editor holds the lock at a time) and observable presence (Filament.Observable — all viewers see current lock status and presence count). The presence count is the number of currently-monitored subscriber PIDs. When a subscriber connects, presence increments. When a subscriber's process dies (:DOWN), presence decrements atomically. Validates: multi-client concurrency, presence as PID count, lock release on disconnect, rung-3 subtree tests with real server. ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run `bw comment "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. Do not improvise. --- ## 0. Prerequisites This ticket requires G2 (observable pattern) and G3 (hold pattern) to be complete. It combines both patterns in a single server. Read before writing: - Track D: how Observable.GenServer manages subscribers (process dict key :__filament_subscribers__), how notify_observers/1 works. - Track E: how Hold.GenServer manages holds (process dict key :__filament_holds__), how handle_acquire/3 and handle_release/3 work. - Track D + E together: can a single GenServer use BOTH macros? Specifically: do their injected handle_info(:DOWN, ...) clauses conflict? This is the key design question. Resolve it before writing any code. If using both macros in one module causes a conflict (e.g., duplicate handle_info :DOWN clauses), the solution is to use only one macro and implement the other functionality manually. See §3 below for the recommended approach. Also add "examples/collaboration/lib" to elixirc_paths(:test) in filament/mix.exs. --- ## 1. Add examples/collaboration/lib to elixirc_paths FILE: filament/mix.exs (final elixirc_paths(:test) state after all G tickets) ```elixir defp elixirc_paths(:test) do [ "lib", "test/support", "examples/todo/lib", "examples/cart/lib", "examples/inventory/lib", "examples/collaboration/lib" # add this line ] end ``` --- ## 2. examples/collaboration/mix.exs Same structure as the other example mix.exs files. App name :collaboration. --- ## 3. Domain — Document.Server design FILE: examples/collaboration/lib/collaboration/document_server.ex CRITICAL DESIGN NOTE: Observable.GenServer and Hold.GenServer both inject a handle_info/2 clause for {:DOWN, ref, :process, pid, reason}. Using both macros in the same module will produce a duplicate clause compiler error. Recommended approach: Use ONLY `use Filament.Observable.GenServer`. Implement hold management manually in the same GenServer using the same process-dictionary key (:__filament_holds__) that Hold.GenServer uses, OR track holds in the server state map. If tracking holds in server state (simpler): the server state contains both subscriber info (managed by Observable.GenServer macro) and lock state (managed manually). The :DOWN handler injected by Observable.GenServer handles subscriber cleanup. We extend it by also checking if the dying process holds the lock, and if so, releasing it. However, the Observable.GenServer :DOWN handler may not be extensible. Read Track D's implementation to check whether it has a callback for custom :DOWN handling (like a `handle_down/3` callback), or whether you must override handle_info/2. If neither macro allows extension, implement BOTH mechanisms manually without using either macro. This is more code but avoids the conflict. Document which path you took and why in a comment at the top of the file. RECOMMENDED STATE SHAPE: ```elixir # Server state (NOT the process dict — plain map in GenServer state) %{ doc_id: String.t(), content: String.t(), lock_holder: nil | pid(), # pid holding the edit lock, or nil presence: non_neg_integer() # number of active subscriber pids } ``` The Observable state (what subscribers see) is a projection of this: ```elixir %{ locked: boolean(), # lock_holder != nil lock_holder: nil | pid(), presence: non_neg_integer() } ``` --- ```elixir defmodule Collaboration.DocumentServer do use Filament.Observable.GenServer # Do NOT also use Filament.Hold.GenServer — see design note above. defstruct [:doc_id, content: "", lock_holder: nil, presence: 0] def start_link(opts \\ []) do doc_id = Keyword.fetch!(opts, :doc_id) name = Keyword.get(opts, :name, via_registry(doc_id)) GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, doc_id, name: name) end # Public API def acquire_lock(server, holder_pid) do GenServer.call(server, {:acquire_lock, holder_pid}) end def release_lock(server, holder_pid) do GenServer.call(server, {:release_lock, holder_pid}) end def get_state(server) do GenServer.call(server, :get_state) end # GenServer callbacks @impl GenServer def init(doc_id) do {:ok, %__MODULE__{doc_id: doc_id}} end # Observable callback — called when a subscriber joins. # Increment presence, call notify_observers to update everyone. @impl Filament.Observable def handle_subscribe(_request, _subscriber, state) do new_state = %{state | presence: state.presence + 1} # Return the current observable view to the new subscriber. initial_view = observable_view(new_state) # Notify existing subscribers of the presence change. notify_observers(initial_view) {:ok, initial_view, new_state} end # Override handle_unsubscribe if Filament.Observable provides it. # Otherwise handle :DOWN manually (see below). # Check Track D for whether handle_unsubscribe/2 is a callback. @impl Filament.Observable def handle_unsubscribe(subscriber_pid, state) do new_state = state |> maybe_release_lock(subscriber_pid) |> decrement_presence() notify_observers(observable_view(new_state)) {:ok, new_state} end @impl GenServer def handle_call({:acquire_lock, holder_pid}, _from, state) do case state.lock_holder do nil -> new_state = %{state | lock_holder: holder_pid} notify_observers(observable_view(new_state)) {:reply, {:ok, :lock_token}, new_state} _ -> {:reply, {:error, :locked}, state} end end @impl GenServer def handle_call({:release_lock, holder_pid}, _from, state) do if state.lock_holder == holder_pid do new_state = %{state | lock_holder: nil} notify_observers(observable_view(new_state)) {:reply, :ok, new_state} else {:reply, {:error, :not_holder}, state} end end @impl GenServer def handle_call(:get_state, _from, state) do {:reply, state, state} end # Private helpers defp observable_view(%__MODULE__{} = state) do %{ locked: state.lock_holder != nil, lock_holder: state.lock_holder, presence: state.presence } end defp maybe_release_lock(state, pid) do if state.lock_holder == pid, do: %{state | lock_holder: nil}, else: state end defp decrement_presence(state) do %{state | presence: max(0, state.presence - 1)} end defp via_registry(doc_id) do {:via, Registry, {Collaboration.Registry, doc_id}} end end ``` NOTE on handle_unsubscribe: Track D's Observable.GenServer handles :DOWN by removing the subscriber from the process dict. It may or may not call a handle_unsubscribe callback. Read Track D's implementation carefully. If handle_unsubscribe/2 does not exist as a callback, you need to override handle_info/2 for {:DOWN, ...} in this module — BUT that will conflict with the injected clause. If overriding handle_info/2 is not possible (depends on Track D's macro), the alternative is: do NOT use `use Filament.Observable.GenServer`. Instead, copy the subscriber management logic from Track D's macro and implement everything manually. This is more code (~60 lines) but avoids all macro conflicts. If this path is taken, document it clearly in the module. --- ## 4. UI — DocumentEditor component FILE: examples/collaboration/lib/collaboration_web/components/document_editor.ex DocumentEditor uses both use_observable (to see lock status and presence) and acquires the lock directly on mount (then renders the editor if lock was acquired, or a read-only view if locked by someone else). NOTE: The lock acquisition on mount is NOT done via use_hold/3 in this example. Instead, it calls DocumentServer.acquire_lock/2 directly from an event closure (clicking "Edit"). This is intentional — it demonstrates manual lock management for cases where hold semantics are more complex than use_hold/3 covers. ```elixir defmodule CollaborationWeb.Components.DocumentEditor do use Filament.Component prop :doc_id, :string, required: true prop :server, :any, required: true def render(assigns) do # Subscribe to lock status and presence count. doc_view = use_observable(assigns.server) ~F"""
<%= presence_label(doc_view) %> here
<%= if doc_view == :uninitialized do %>

Connecting…

<% else %>
<%= if doc_view.locked do %> 🔒 Locked by another user <% else %> <% end %>
<% end %>
""" end defp presence_label(:uninitialized), do: "…" defp presence_label(%{presence: 1}), do: "1 user" defp presence_label(%{presence: n}), do: "#{n} users" end ``` --- ## 5. Test: verify Document.Server lock and presence behavior FILE: test/filament/examples/collaboration_test.exs ```elixir defmodule Filament.Examples.CollaborationTest do use ExUnit.Case, async: true alias Collaboration.DocumentServer defp start_server(doc_id \\ "test-doc") do {:ok, server} = DocumentServer.start_link(doc_id: doc_id) server end test "acquire lock succeeds when unlocked" do server = start_server() assert {:ok, :lock_token} = DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self()) state = DocumentServer.get_state(server) assert state.lock_holder == self() end test "acquire lock returns {:error, :locked} when already held" do server = start_server() other_pid = spawn(fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end) assert {:ok, _} = DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, other_pid) assert {:error, :locked} = DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self()) Process.exit(other_pid, :kill) end test "lock is released when holder process dies" do server = start_server() parent = self() holder = spawn(fn -> {:ok, _} = DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self()) send(parent, :acquired) receive do: (:die -> :ok) end) assert_receive :acquired, 500 assert DocumentServer.get_state(server).lock_holder == holder Process.exit(holder, :kill) Process.sleep(100) # wait for :DOWN to propagate state = DocumentServer.get_state(server) assert state.lock_holder == nil end test "presence count reflects active subscribers" do # This test requires the Filament.Observable.subscribe/3 low-level API. # If not available, use Filament.Test.mount/2 from Track F instead. # Mark @tag :pending if Track F is not yet merged. server = start_server() sub = %Filament.Observable.Subscriber{ pid: self(), fiber_id: :collab_test, slot_index: 0, project: &Function.identity/1, last_projected: :unset, ref: make_ref() } {:ok, initial} = Filament.Observable.subscribe(server, nil, sub) assert initial.presence == 1 # Unsubscribe should decrement presence. Filament.Observable.unsubscribe(server, self()) Process.sleep(50) state = DocumentServer.get_state(server) assert state.presence == 0 end test "DocumentEditor component module exists" do assert Code.ensure_loaded?(CollaborationWeb.Components.DocumentEditor) end end ``` --- ## Completion criteria 1. `mix compile` succeeds from `examples/collaboration/` (standalone). 2. `mix compile` succeeds from `filament/` with updated elixirc_paths. 3. `mix test test/filament/examples/collaboration_test.exs` passes all 5 tests (or passes non-pending tests, with pending tests documented). 4. No compiler warnings. 5. The "both macros conflict" design question is resolved and documented in a comment at the top of document_server.ex.
title: G4: Collaboration locks example — Document.Server with pessimistic lock + presence count
